events.event: Jean Baptiste Point du Sable, born in Saint-Domingue (Haiti), establishes his trading settlement in Chicago; he is recognized as the city's first non-Indigenous settler and founder.
Quinn congregation organizes as an AME congregation in Chicago, named for Bishop William Paul Quinn.
North Star Lodge of Chicago organized by the Ohio Jurisdiction of Prince Hall Masons.
Illinois Grand Lodge of Prince Hall Masons organized.
Provident Hospital founded in Chicago by Dr. Daniel Hale Williams — first Black-owned/operated hospital in the U.S.
Wells flees Memphis for Chicago
events.description: A mob destroys Ida B. Wells's Free Speech office; she settles in Chicago and works with the Chicago Conservator.

events.event: Frederick Douglass is appointed commissioner to Haiti's pavilion at the World's Columbian Exposition; on January 2, 1893 he delivers his 'Lecture on Haiti' at the Haitian Pavilion dedication in Chicago.
Ida B. Wells moves to Chicago (1893) and tours Britain as an anti-lynching speaker (1893, 1894).
The Broad Ax published in Salt Lake City (Aug 1895–mid-1899); moves to Chicago in 1899.
National Association of Colored Women's second convention convenes at Quinn Chapel, Chicago (Aug 14–16, 1899).
Chicago Defender founded
events.description: Robert S. Abbott begins publishing the Defender in Chicago.

events.event: First issue of the Chicago Defender published by Robert S. Abbott.
Wells opens the Negro Fellowship League Reading Room and Social Center in Chicago.
NAACP adds its first two branches in Boston and Chicago.
entity_names: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP)

events.event: Wells founds the Alpha Suffrage Club in Chicago; marches in the Woman Suffrage Procession in Washington, D.C.
National Baptist Convention annual meeting in Chicago splits: Boyd's supporters form the National Baptist Convention of America.
ASNLH founded at the Wabash Avenue YMCA, Chicago.
entity_names: Association for the Study of Negro Life and History (ASNLH/ASALH)

events.event: ASNLH incorporated in Washington, D.C.
entity_names: Association for the Study of Negro Life and History (ASNLH/ASALH)

events.event: Chicago Urban League organized; Dorsey migrates
events.description: The Chicago Urban League organizes at the Wabash Avenue YMCA (Dec 11, 1916) to aid Southern migrants; Thomas A. Dorsey first migrates to Chicago.

events.event: ANP founded; Garvey visits; Oliver arrives
events.description: Claude Barnett founds the Associated Negro Press in Chicago (Mar 2); Marcus Garvey addresses Chicago's UNIA (Sep 28); King Oliver arrives in Chicago; Dorsey settles permanently.

events.event: Associated Negro Press founded in Chicago by Claude Barnett.
The UNIA, founded in Jamaica by Marcus Garvey in 1914, has several Chicago divisions by 1920, principally on the South Side, with weekly Liberty Hall meetings and businesses.
UNIA Division 23 founded in Chicago; delegate William A. Wallace attends the First International Convention in Harlem.
Armstrong summoned to Chicago
events.description: King Oliver sends for Louis Armstrong in New Orleans; Armstrong joins the Creole Jazz Band in Chicago.

events.event: Cole family to Chicago; Poole family to Detroit
events.description: The Nat King Cole family moves Montgomery, AL to Chicago (Bronzeville); Elijah Poole's family moves Georgia to Detroit.

events.event: Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters founded
events.description: A. Philip Randolph founds the BSCP; Milton P. Webster and John C. Mills build the Chicago division.

events.event: Noble Drew Ali moves Moorish Science Temple headquarters from Newark to Chicago.
Mahalia Jackson and Richard Wright reach Chicago
events.description: Mahalia Jackson moves New Orleans to Chicago (1927; one source says 1928); Richard Wright leaves Memphis for Chicago on December 27, 1927.

events.event: Moorish National Conclave held in Chicago.
Archibald Motley receives a Guggenheim Fellowship and spends 1929–early 1930 in Paris, where he paints Blues.
events.evidence: Nasher Museum (Duke) and Whitney Museum document the fellowship, the Paris stay, and the painting.

events.event: J.A. Rogers attends the coronation of Haile Selassie in Ethiopia.
events.description: Per AALBC biography.

events.event: Dorsey institutionalizes gospel
events.description: Dorsey becomes Pilgrim Baptist music director and co-founds the National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses.

events.event: Cooke family to Chicago
events.description: The Sam Cooke family moves Clarksdale, MS to Chicago.

events.event: First session of the National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses at Pilgrim Baptist Church, Chicago.
entity_names: National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses (NCGCC)

events.event: NOI headquarters Detroit to Chicago
events.description: After Fard's disappearance, Elijah Muhammad relocates the Nation of Islam's leadership to Chicago.

events.event: Elijah Muhammad moves Nation of Islam followers from Detroit to Chicago; Temple No. 2 becomes headquarters.
Pittsburgh Courier sends J.A. Rogers to Ethiopia to cover the Italian invasion — the only African-American journalist on the ground.
events.description: Covered Ethiopia for the Courier 1935-36; also wrote regularly for the Chicago Defender.

events.event: Donald Pierson's Salvador fieldwork
events.description: University of Chicago PhD student Donald Pierson lives in Salvador, Bahia, researching Black–white relations.

events.event: Willie Dixon to Chicago
events.description: Willie Dixon moves Vicksburg, MS to Chicago.

events.event: Gladneys to Chicago
events.description: Ida Mae and George Gladney migrate from Chickasaw County, MS to Chicago.

events.event: Robert E. Park's six-week visit to Brazil
events.description: Park supervises Pierson's fieldwork in Salvador; the visit links the Chicago school of sociology to Afro-Brazilian race-relations research.

events.event: Dunham creates Bahiana and Batucada
events.description: Katherine Dunham creates the Brazilian/Bahian-themed works Bahiana (1939) and Batucada (1940), the latter appearing in Warner Bros.' Carnival of Rhythm (1941).

events.event: Substantial Belizean migration to Chicago begins: domestic workers on the North Shore, recruits from Florida citrus work, and Farm Work Program/War Manpower Commission workers; Belizeans settle along Howard Street in Rogers Park and in Evanston.
Ramos–Herskovits reciprocal honors
events.description: Herskovits becomes honorary professor of Bahia's Faculty of Philosophy; Arthur Ramos becomes honorary member of Northwestern's Anthropology Research Association, amid an exchange of works.

events.event: Herskovitses' Bahia fieldwork
events.description: Melville and Frances Herskovits conduct Rockefeller-funded fieldwork in Bahia, including among Gantois Candomblé members.

events.event: Negroes in Brazil published
events.description: The University of Chicago Press publishes Pierson's Negroes in Brazil: A Study of Race Contact at Bahia, with Park's introduction; it wins an Anisfield Award.

events.event: Hughes's Chicago Defender column
events.description: Langston Hughes writes a weekly column for the Chicago Defender, 1942–1962, covering race, politics, and international affairs.

events.event: Muddy Waters to Chicago; Simple debuts
events.description: Muddy Waters moves Stovall Plantation, MS to Chicago; Langston Hughes's 'Simple' debuts in the Chicago Defender (February).

events.event: National Baptist Convention annual session in Chicago (Sep 7–12): U.S. Armory, Olivet, Pilgrim, Monumental Baptist.
Black Metropolis published; Ebony founded
events.description: Drake and Cayton publish Black Metropolis (Wright introduction); John H. Johnson launches Ebony in Chicago.

events.event: Sun Ra reaches Chicago
events.description: Sun Ra arrives in Chicago from Birmingham, AL, in early 1946.

events.event: Richard Wright first visits Paris as a guest of the French government.
events.evidence: Wright chronology records the May 1946 visit.

events.event: Era Bell Thompson joins Ebony magazine in Chicago.
events.description: Begins the career that made her Ebony's Africa foreign correspondent.

events.event: Richard Wright settles permanently in France with his family.
events.evidence: Tommie Shelby's chapter (citing the University of Chicago Press biography) and the Wright chronology document the 1947 permanent move.

events.event: Alice Dunnigan becomes head of the ANP Washington Bureau.
Cuba Libre: first English translations of Guillén
events.description: Hughes and Ben F. Carruthers publish the first English translations of Nicolás Guillén's poetry as Cuba Libre (Anderson & Ritchie).

events.event: Katherine Dunham's company makes its first European tour, including London, with return engagements in France and Italy.
events.evidence: Harvard repository document records the 1948 tour and returns.

events.event: Gillespie/Pozo at the Pershing Ballroom, Chicago
events.description: Dizzy Gillespie's big band, featuring Chano Pozo on conga with guests Miles Davis and Charlie Parker, performs at Chicago's Pershing Ballroom (audience recording).

events.event: Margaret Walker returns South
events.description: Walker joins the English faculty at Jackson State College, MS - a named Chicago-to-South return migration.

events.event: Aristocrat becomes Chess Records
events.description: Leonard and Phil Chess rename their Chicago label Chess Records.

events.event: Dunham refused lodging in São Paulo
events.description: Katherine Dunham's reservation at São Paulo's Hotel Esplanada is refused because she is Black; she denounces the episode publicly during her Municipal Theater performances (Correio Paulistano, July 11–13, 1950).

events.event: Jet founded
events.description: John H. Johnson launches Jet magazine in Chicago.

events.event: Big Bill Broonzy makes his first European tour (invited by French critic Hugues Panassié); he returns in 1955 and 1957.
events.evidence: Encyclopedia of Arkansas records the 1951, 1955, and 1957 tours; Blues Chronicles names Panassié.

events.event: Lei Afonso Arinos enacted
events.description: Brazil's Law 1.390, the country's first anti-racial-discrimination statute, is enacted following the press scandal over Dunham's treatment.

events.event: Howlin' Wolf to Chicago
events.description: Howlin' Wolf relocates from West Memphis to Chicago after Sam Phillips leases his recordings to Leonard Chess.

events.event: Vee-Jay Records founded
events.description: Vivian Carter and Jimmy Bracken launch Vee-Jay, the leading Black-owned label before Motown.

events.event: Era Bell Thompson travels through 18 African countries for 'Africa, Land of My Fathers.'
events.description: Documented by African American Registry and Rutgers dissertation.

events.event: 'One Tenth of a Nation – The Press' newsreel documents the ANP's Chicago headquarters and its Washington, UN, London, New York, and Africa correspondents.
Emperor Haile Selassie I of Ethiopia visits Chicago: Midway arrival, Mayor Kennelly greeting, Drake Hotel stay, ~25,000 lining the motorcade route.
events.description: First reigning emperor to visit Chicago, per academic account; young UChicago student Donald Levine watched the motorcade.

events.event: Haitian president Paul Magloire visits Chicago, reported in the Atlanta Daily World on February 9, 1955, during a 1934–1956 era of Haiti–Chicago cultural and political exchange.
'Bo Diddley' recorded in Chicago
events.description: 'Bo Diddley'/'I'm a Man' (Checker 814) is recorded at Universal Recording Studio, 46 E. Walton Street, Chicago, and released in March 1955.

events.event: Ethel Payne covers the Bandung Conference for the Chicago Defender.
'Maybellene' recorded
events.description: Chuck Berry records 'Maybellene' for Chess in Chicago after Muddy Waters's referral.

events.event: Emmett Till murdered
events.description: Chicago youth Emmett Till is abducted and murdered near Money, Mississippi, while visiting relatives.

events.event: Emmett Till's funeral at Roberts Temple COGIC, Chicago; body returned from Mississippi. Jet/Ebony publish open-casket photos.
entity_names: Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ

events.event: Jet publishes Till funeral photos
events.description: Jet's September 15 issue carries David Jackson's open-casket photographs, with Mamie Till-Mobley's permission.

events.event: Era Bell Thompson jailed overnight in South Africa during a reporting trip.
events.description: Single biographical source; provisional detail.

events.event: Ghanaian independence celebrations: the Barnetts attend; Etta Moten Barnett interviews Martin Luther King Jr. Ethel Payne accompanies Nixon to Ghana.
Muddy Waters tours the UK with Chris Barber's band and Otis Spann.
events.evidence: uDiscover Music reports the 1958 UK tour.

events.event: Claude Barnett attends the All-African People's Conference in Accra, Ghana.
Malcolm X travels to Egypt and Saudi Arabia as a Nation of Islam emissary; his reports appear in the Pittsburgh Courier.
events.description: Peer-reviewed (MDPI) via Essien-Udom.

events.event: Jet magazine (Chicago) puts Kenyan leader Tom Mboya on its cover ('Africa's New Leader') during his U.S. tour.
events.description: Chicago-Africa media link; no evidence Mboya visited Chicago (negative finding).

events.event: European premiere of Lorraine Hansberry's A Raisin in the Sun at the Bristol Hippodrome, followed by London's Adelphi Theatre from 4 August 1959.
events.evidence: Humanists UK records the Bristol premiere date and Adelphi transfer.

events.event: Elijah Muhammad's world tour: Turkey, Pakistan, Syria, Sudan, Egypt, Ethiopia, Lebanon, Jordan, Saudi Arabia (Umrah); NOI account reports a meeting with Nasser.
events.description: Itinerary peer-reviewed; Nasser meeting provisional (NOI's own account).

events.event: Chicago Daily Defender publishes 'Massacre in South Africa' on the Sharpeville massacre.
events.description: Quoted in Georgetown thesis.

events.event: ANP release publishes responses from Liberian president William V. S. Tubman and Senator John F. Kennedy.
Richard Wright dies in Paris; buried in Père-Lachaise cemetery.
events.evidence: Wright chronology records the death date and burial.

events.event: Ghanaian college students in Chicago form the Ghana Students' Union, precursor of the Ghana National Council.
events.description: Per peer-reviewed Migration Letters article.
entity_names: Ghana National Council of Metropolitan Chicago

events.event: Hurricane Hattie devastates Belize; another substantial wave of Belizean immigrants arrives in Chicago.
Muhammad Speaks moves from Harlem to Chicago.
Hooker records 'Burnin'' in Chicago
events.description: Detroit-based John Lee Hooker cuts the Burnin' album in Chicago for Vee-Jay.

events.event: Memphis Slim moves permanently to Paris.
events.evidence: Archived liner notes document the 1962 permanent move.

events.event: First American Folk Blues Festival: Paris Olympia (20 Oct), then Manchester Free Trade Hall (21 Oct, the only UK date).
events.evidence: Louder's festival history gives the 1962 routing and dates.

events.event: The Rolling Stones record at Chess Studios, Chicago (10–11 June 1964).
events.evidence: Elsewhere quotes Wyman and Watts on the Chess session.

events.event: The Rolling Stones release their cover of Willie Dixon's 'Little Red Rooster' as a UK single; it reaches No. 1 in December 1964.
events.evidence: Facility Fun and Men's Journal (citing uDiscover Music) document the release and chart peak.

events.event: Chicago Freedom Movement
events.description: SCLC joins Chicago's CCCO: North Lawndale apartment (Jan), Freedom Sunday at Soldier Field (Jul 10), Marquette Park marches (Aug), Summit Agreement (Aug 26).

events.event: First Puerto Rican Day Parade, Chicago
events.description: Chicago's first Puerto Rican Day Parade is held downtown during the first Puerto Rico Week.

events.event: Division Street uprising
events.description: After police shoot Arcelis Cruz, three days of uprising on Division Street catalyze Puerto Rican and pan-Latino institution-building in Chicago.

events.event: Haki Madhubuti founds Third World Press in a South Side Chicago basement with Carolyn Rodgers and Johari Amini.
events.description: Founding-month detail provisional (Wikipedia-derived); Chicago founding well corroborated.

events.event: King assassinated; Mahalia sings; Staples sign Stax
events.description: MLK assassinated in Memphis (Apr 4); Mahalia Jackson sings at his Atlanta funeral; the Chicago-based Staple Singers sign with Memphis's Stax Records.

events.event: AfriCOBRA founded in Chicago.
events.description: Smithsonian AAA.

events.event: Nelson Harold Rogers meets ANC members in Tanzania; they ask him to establish a Midwest ANC chapter.
events.description: Rogers's testimony; chapter established early 1970s.

events.event: Chicago's first Rainbow Coalition
events.description: The Illinois Black Panther Party, the Young Lords, and the Young Patriots form the Rainbow Coalition.

events.event: Fleetwood Mac record with Chicago blues musicians at Chess's Ter-Mar studio, Chicago; released by UK label Blue Horizon in December 1969.
events.evidence: Discogs documents the session date, studio, personnel, and Blue Horizon release.

events.event: Art Ensemble of Chicago records Message to Our Folks at Studio Saravah, Paris, for BYG Records.
events.evidence: BYG Records' release page states the August 1969 Studio Saravah recording.

events.event: Sun Ra's first concerts outside the US: France, Germany, and the UK (late summer/autumn 1970).
events.evidence: Strut Records liner notes document the first non-US concerts.

events.event: Howlin' Wolf records The London Howlin' Wolf Sessions at Olympic Sound Studios, London, with Clapton, Winwood, Wyman, and Watts.
events.evidence: Discogs documents the May 1970 London recording and personnel.

events.event: Melida Harris Barrow begins the First Chicago Caribbean Carnival at Lincoln Park; it continues for over 20 years.
Jesse Jackson founds Operation PUSH in Chicago.
events.description: Merged with the National Rainbow Coalition in 1996.

events.event: Segundo Ruiz Belvis Cultural Center founded
events.description: SRBCC is established, becoming Chicago's longest-running Latino/Latine cultural center.

events.event: BYG/Actuel releases Sun Ra's The Solar-Myth Approach Vol. 1 & 2; Sun Ra's second European tour ends with December 1971 Egypt recordings.
events.evidence: Soundohm documents the BYG/Actuel releases; Strut liner notes document the tour and Egypt recordings.

events.event: Operation PUSH founded
events.description: Jesse Jackson founds Operation PUSH in Chicago.

events.event: Puerto Rican Cultural Center founded
events.description: The PRCC is established by Chicago's Puerto Rican/Latina/o community in Humboldt Park.
entity_names: Puerto Rican Cultural Center (Juan Antonio Corretjer)

events.event: CCICS Nile Valley study tour: Dakar (Cheikh Anta Diop lectures), Khartoum (Yusuf Fadl Hassan lecture), Nairobi, Cairo, Aswan.
events.description: Participant account by Josef Ben Levi.

events.event: FESTAC '77 in Lagos, Nigeria: AfriCOBRA invited; Donaldson leads North American-zone delegation; Jarrell chairs the dress committee; National Theatre Gallery exhibition.
events.description: Peer-reviewed (Civilisations).

events.event: Kemetic Institute of Chicago founded at the Center for Inner City Studies, with Jacob Carruthers's intellectual thrust.
events.description: Institutional outcome of the 1977 study tour.

events.event: Bob Marley & The Wailers play the Uptown Theatre in Chicago on the Kaya Tour; audience recording and set list survive.
entity_names: Bob Marley & The Wailers at the Uptown Theatre (May 27, 1978)

events.event: Jesse Jackson visits South Africa and publicly denounces apartheid.
events.description: Multiple news/biographical sources.

events.event: Chicago signs sister-city agreement with Casablanca, Morocco.
events.description: CSCI record.

events.event: Chicago-area CALC/TransAfrica Krugerrand campaign: mayoral candidates Harold Washington and Bernard Epton pledge city-funds withdrawal; First National Bank of Chicago stops selling Krugerrands.
events.description: Harvard Crimson, 1983.

events.event: Center for Black Music Research founded
events.description: Samuel A. Floyd founds the CBMR at Columbia College Chicago, devoted to Black music worldwide.

events.event: Ethiopian Community Association of Chicago founded by Ethiopian immigrants.
events.description: IRS listing gives July 1985 incorporation; treated as incorporation vs founding.

events.event: Ghana Students' Union becomes the Ghana National Council umbrella organization.
events.description: Migration Letters.
entity_names: Ghana National Council of Metropolitan Chicago

events.event: Alderman Danny K. Davis submits 'Resolution Condemning Apartheid' to the Chicago City Council.
events.description: Primary archival document.

events.event: Free South Africa Coalition Youth Committee flyer: 'Chicago Youth Say No to Apartheid and Racism!'
events.description: Primary archival flyer.

events.event: Gaddafi addresses the NOI's Saviours' Day in Chicago by satellite and provides a reported $5 million interest-free loan.
events.description: Provisional; secondary/partisan sources.

events.event: The Wild Hare reggae venue opens at 3530 N. Clark, Chicago, under owner-musician Zeleke Gessesse; it runs 25 years.

Farley 'Jackmaster' Funk's 'Love Can't Turn Around' reaches UK No. 10; Marshall Jefferson's 'Move Your Body' (Trax TX117) reaches UK No. 7; The House Sound of Chicago compilation circulates in the UK via London Records; the Haçienda's 'Nude' nights begin playing Chicago house.
events.evidence: MusicVF (Farley), HipHopElectronic/Jahsonic (Jefferson), YouTube discographic upload (compilation), Decoded Magazine/Wikipedia (Haçienda).

events.event: Ga-Dangme Homowo Festival of Thanksgiving held in Chicago — the precursor of GhanaFest.
events.description: Renamed GhanaFest in 1990; founding-year accounts vary (1987/1988/1990).
entity_names: Ghana National Council of Metropolitan Chicago

events.event: Steve 'Silk' Hurley's 'Jack Your Body' begins two weeks at No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart.
events.evidence: True House Stories reports the two-week No. 1 run from 18 January 1987.

events.event: Chicago Concerned Jamaicans is established in Chicago for Hurricane Gilbert relief, beginning sustained transnational philanthropy to Jamaican education.
Memphis Slim dies in Paris.
events.evidence: Archived liner notes record the death date and place.

events.event: Patrick Woodtor founds Africa International House in Chicago.
events.description: Congressional Record, 2022.

events.event: Chicago-Accra sister-city relationship established.
events.description: CSCI announcement.

events.event: Lil Louis's 'French Kiss' reaches UK No. 2; Italy's Black Box releases 'Ride on Time', sampling Chicago-born Loleatta Holloway's 'Love Sensation' without clearance (she sues).
events.evidence: MusicVF (French Kiss); NME (Black Box/Holloway).

events.event: Louis H. Ford becomes Presiding Bishop of the Church of God in Christ (headquartered in Memphis).
Chicago Sister Cities program created
events.description: Mayor Richard M. Daley's Executive Order 1990-90-1 creates the citywide sister-cities program.

events.event: Chicago City Council passes anti-apartheid banking/selective-purchasing ordinance (effective October 31, 1990); Alderwoman Helen Shiller instrumental.
events.description: Anti-Apartheid Newsletter (MSU archive).

events.event: Sun Ra returns to Birmingham
events.description: After a 1990 stroke, Sun Ra returns to Birmingham for family care and dies there in 1993.

events.event: Chicago–Mexico City sister city (est.)
events.description: Chicago–Mexico City sister-city relationship established (25th anniversary marked in 2016).

events.event: Nelson Mandela's Chicago visit: 2.5 days, six fundraising events, organized by Nelson Harold Rogers with the Chicago Free South Africa Movement.
events.description: Visit corroborated by Northwestern Now; duration/fundraiser count from Rogers's testimony.

events.event: Ephraim Malachi Martin establishes the African/Caribbean International Festival of Life in Chicago (first at Hawthorne Park Racetrack); DJ Chuck Wren founds the ska/reggae/rocksteady/calypso label Jump Up Records in Chicago.
First Fiesta Boricua
events.description: The Puerto Rican Cultural Center launches Fiesta Boricua on Paseo Boricua (PRCC dates it to 1993; edition numbering implies 1994).
entity_names: Puerto Rican Cultural Center (Juan Antonio Corretjer)

events.event: Celia Cruz at the Aragon Ballroom
events.description: Celia Cruz performs at Chicago's Aragon Ballroom.

events.event: Paseo Boricua flags erected
events.description: The two monumental steel Puerto Rican flags are installed over Division Street in Humboldt Park.

events.event: Puerto Rican Arts Alliance founded
events.description: Carlos Hernández Falcón founds PRAA (Illinois House resolution says 1996; some accounts say 1998).

events.event: Roy Davis Jr. releases 'Gabrielle' (with Peven Everett) on Chicago's Large Records; DJ Rush moves from Chicago to Berlin.
events.evidence: Discogs (Large Records 1996); DJ Rush's Berlin move dated 1996 by Wikipedia and confirmed as lived experience in his Tanzgemeinschaft interview.

events.event: Chicago-Durban sister-city relationship established.
events.description: CSCI announcement.

events.event: UK label XL Recordings releases Roy Davis Jr.'s 'Gabriel'; it reaches UK No. 22 in November 1997.
events.evidence: Discogs documents the XL release; chart details from discographic summaries.

events.event: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture founded
events.description: Chicago Puerto Rican community activists, artists, and educators found the museum.
entity_names: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture

events.event: Northwestern's CaribNation holds the third annual CaribFest (May 2002, featuring Chicago reggae band Indika) and fourth annual CaribFest (May 2003, featuring Evanston Haitian band Sakad).
Ephraim Malachi Martin launches the Caribbean Festival (CAF) in Chicago's north and west loop areas.
United African Organization founded in Chicago.
events.description: Migration Letters.

events.event: São Paulo declares sister-city relationship with Chicago
events.description: São Paulo Municipal Law 14.112 declares Chicago and São Paulo 'Cidades Irmãs.'

events.event: U.S. Senator Barack Obama (D-IL) visits Kenya on a two-week Africa tour (South Africa, Kenya, Chad, Djibouti).
events.description: NPR, VOA, AFP contemporaneous coverage.

events.event: UK label Planet Mu releases Bangs & Works Vol. 1 (A Chicago Footwork Compilation); the follow-up enables a UK/European tour by DJs Rashad and Spinn with footwork dancers.
events.evidence: Planet Mu's own release pages give the date, roster, and tour.

events.event: Haitian-born Elsie Hector Hernandez founds the Haitian American Museum of Chicago in Uptown.
Theaster Gates presents 12 Ballads for Huguenot House at dOCUMENTA 13, Kassel, Germany, using materials from 6901 South Dorchester, Chicago.
events.evidence: Nonsite and Wallpaper document the project and materials.

events.event: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture opens
events.description: The museum opens in the historic Humboldt Park stables.
entity_names: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture

events.event: Frankie Knuckles plays his final gig at London's Ministry of Sound, then returns to Chicago, where he dies.
events.evidence: His manager Judy Weinstein's account in the public-radio documentary 'Where Love Lives'.

events.event: Chicago Latino Theater Alliance founded
events.description: CLATA is founded through collaboration among the National Museum of Mexican Art, the International Latino Cultural Center, and PRAA.

events.event: Ephraim Malachi Martin launches the Jerk, Seafood & Vegan Fest in downtown Chicago/South Loop.
Ethiopian Airlines begins Chicago O'Hare-Addis Ababa service — first scheduled direct Chicago-Africa passenger service.
events.description: City of Chicago announcement.

events.event: Kwame Raoul, born in Chicago to Haitian immigrants, takes office as the 42nd Illinois attorney general.
San Juan to Chicago: Un Puente Musical
events.description: The Chicago Philharmonic and PRAA present the collaboration led by Roselín Pabón.

events.event: La Creación premiered
events.description: Chucho Valdés's Afro-Cuban suite La Creación, co-commissioned by Chicago's Symphony Center, premieres in Miami.

events.event: Jamaica's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade confirms Lester Barclay as Honorary Consul of Jamaica in Chicago.
Progressive National Baptist Convention 64th Annual Session in Chicago (Jul 20–23, McCormick Place, ~2,000 delegates).
The Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago presents 'Dancing the Revolution: From Dancehall to Reggaetón,' curated by Carla Acevedo-Yates, on Jamaican dancehall and reggaetón through contemporary art.
entity_names: Dancing the Revolution: From Dancehall to Reggaetón (MCA Chicago)

events.event: 37th Annual GhanaFest held in Washington Park, Chicago.
events.description: todaygh; GIPC chairman guest of honor.
